adjudication.basis: Most of the evening is routine command access and listening. The consequential uncertainty is whether Ned's blunt warning can influence Robert without rupturing cooperation. Robert therefore accepts the command principle and keeps cooperation intact, while refusing to promise that he will avoid Rhaegar or personal danger.
adjudication.opposition: Robert retains his own authority, pride, anger toward Rhaegar, and preference for personal frontline action. Ned cannot command Robert to remain safe or dictate Robert's private motives.
adjudication.preparation: Ned has private access to Robert as his foster brother and close friend, shared battlefield history, a legitimate command interest in northern casualties, and a warning framed around the rebellion's collective military needs.
adjudication.risk: A badly received rebuke could sour immediate coordination or cause Robert to dismiss the warning. Even a well received warning cannot guarantee Robert's conduct once the battle begins.

input.narrative:
Jory comes when Ned sends for him. Ned does not call a general northern council. He tells Jory to bring the lords to him one at a time, with enough space between them that each man can speak without the next waiting inside the tent. Jory sends runners through the northern lanes of the camp and returns with the order understood. The first lord arrives while weapon work is still going on outside.

Ned keeps the meetings practical. He asks where each man's companies are quartered, when they last ate, how the watches are divided, whether the horses have been checked, whether the officers know where to find their own banners if the line shifts, and what worries the lord most about the morning. He does not ask for a speech. When drink is brought, he shares a cup and lets the other man talk.

The answers are not uniform. One lord is more concerned with tired men than the royal army. Too many of his rear companies have been awake since before dawn, first on movement and then on camp work. He says they are fresh enough, then asks whether Ned will permit him to change the next watch because half the men assigned to it have already served twice. Another lord wants cleaner messenger arrangements between neighboring commands. He has no wish to see a local success turn into a pursuit that leaves a flank open. A third is less worried about courage than about horses, ground near the river, and men trying to find their own officers once banners and dust begin to move.

Ned makes them separate the things they know from the things they have heard. No man is allowed to improve a scout's report merely because it has passed through three tents. They review the northern arrangements already in hand, who answers to whom, where orders are expected to come from, how men are to rally on their own command if noise or movement breaks contact, and which questions still depend on the final meeting with the other rebel leaders. Ned asks each lord what he thinks his own men will do badly if the day becomes confused. That gets longer answers than asking what they will do well.

He also asks about fear. Some of the answers are military. Men are afraid of being ridden down, losing sight of their banner, or getting trapped at the water. Some are simpler. They have wives north of the Neck, children who know only that their fathers marched south, fields left to brothers, and villages where the work will still need doing if the army wins. No single answer becomes a judgment on the host.

Before each lord leaves, Ned gives the same instruction in plain terms. Necessary watches stay manned. Necessary work gets finished. Everything else stops early enough for men to sleep.

"A tired army is a dead army," he tells one of them. "Do not have them sitting over cups half the night because they are frightened of lying down."

The order goes out through the northern command. It is not an order to abandon sentries, horses, armor checks, or duties that cannot wait. It is an order against making exhaustion into a point of pride.

Ned then goes to Robert.

He asks to speak with him before the larger command meeting, and the two are given the privacy available in a war camp. Ned begins as a friend. He asks Robert what he means to do when the fighting starts, not what the captains expect him to do.

Robert's answer is direct. He intends to be forward with his own men. He will not command the rebellion from a safe place behind everyone else. If Rhaegar comes within reach, Robert says, he will not turn away from him.

Ned lets him finish before answering.

"Then do not play the fool tomorrow," Ned says. "I will not have northern men die because you lose your head over one man. You are the man this rebellion follows. Be calm enough to remember that when the field turns ugly."

Robert's first answer is sharp. He asks whether Ned means to put him behind a baggage wagon while other men fight his war. Ned does not retreat from what he said. He tells Robert that fighting is not the same as throwing command away, and that a personal quarrel does not get to spend northern lives.

The argument does not become a break between them. Robert does not promise to stay out of danger. He does not promise to ignore Rhaegar if the prince is in front of him. He does say that he understands the point Ned is making: the army cannot be bent around his anger, and the other leaders need to know what he is doing before his personal choices create a hole they must fill.

Jon Arryn and Hoster Tully join them for the final coordination.

The four men work through command rather than speeches. They confirm which forces remain under which lord's authority and what information must move between them. They review how a messenger is to identify the order he carries, who sends another if the first does not arrive, and how neighboring commanders are to distinguish a local withdrawal from a general one. They go over rally and hold instructions and the danger of men chasing a broken enemy beyond supporting distance because the first part of a fight has gone well. No one produces a newly certain royal order of battle. Reports that remain reports are kept that way.

Jon presses hardest on cohesion. One contingent cannot assume another has seen the same movement or received the same message. Hoster wants the chain of messengers simple enough to survive losses and confusion. Robert accepts that his movements must be reported, even while he keeps his intention to fight forward. Ned confirms the northern officers will be told to treat signals and orders through recognized command rather than rumor moving along the line.

No wholesale reassignment of the northern host is made in the meeting. The clarifications can go out through runners without bringing the lords back into another long council.

Ned leaves the command meeting and walks the northern lines before he retires.

He does not inspect them as a parade. He stops where men are sitting with gear open, where horses are being checked, and where small groups have not yet broken for sleep. He asks names, homes, family, and what work they expect to return to. One man talks about nets and a father's boat. Another has brothers keeping a holding going without him. A younger man says his mother will complain about the state of his boots before she asks whether he was brave. Ned asks what they have been told about the morning and corrects only what needs correcting. Exact enemy numbers are still not known. The battle is expected, not already won.

The practical work continues around the conversations. A buckle is tightened and tested. A horse's forefoot is lifted, picked clean, and set down. A shield strap is pulled through its fastening and checked against the forearm. Men assigned to the next watch remain awake. Others begin to turn in under their captains' orders.

By the time Ned returns to his command tent, the long round of talking is finished. His field harness is still there for the morning. He has issued no battle action beyond the preparation and command instructions already given. At about half past ten he goes to bed. The expected battle remains for the next day, and nothing after Ned retires is resolved.

character.aim: Help defeat the royal army at the Trident, preserve his northern forces where possible, support Robert and the rebel cause, and survive the coming battle.
character.background: Family: Son of Lord Rickard Stark and Lady Lyarra Stark. Younger brother of Brandon Stark; elder brother of Lyanna and Benjen Stark. Rickard and Brandon are dead by order of King Aerys II. Lyanna is missing. Benjen is alive, but his exact activity at this starting moment is not needed for the opening scene. Upbringing: Raised at Winterfell until age eight, then fostered at the Eyrie under Lord Jon Arryn. Robert Baratheon was his fellow ward and became his close friend. From sixteen onward Ned divided time between Winterfell and the Eyrie. Education: Noble education appropriate to a son of House Stark, including literacy, heraldry, law/custom, riding, arms, command, household obligations, and courtly conduct. Trade / occupation: Landed noble and military commander. No skilled trade is established. Military experience: Formal noble martial training from childhood; active service throughout Robert's Rebellion; called the banners of the North; marched south with the northern host; participated as a commander in the Battle of the Bells, where the rebel relief force helped reverse the battle. Court experience: Long residence in Jon Arryn's household at the Eyrie; exposure to high nobility; attendance at the tourney at Harrenhal. Limited evidence of prolonged royal-court experience. Religious background: Keeps the old gods of the First Men. Important past events: Fosterage at the Eyrie; friendship with Robert; tourney at Harrenhal; disappearance of Lyanna with Rhaegar Targaryen; executions of Rickard and Brandon; Aerys's demand for Ned's and Robert's heads; dangerous return north through the Mountains of the Moon, the Bite, and the Three Sisters; succession as Lord of Winterfell; raising the northern banners; Battle of the Bells; recent marriage to Catelyn Tully at Riverrun.

equipment: At the opening: ordinary campaign clothing, riding boots, and belt worn. No armor, helmet, gauntlets, shield, or battle weapon is worn or readied. No special rank jewelry is assumed.
Plain serviceable steel longsword across Ned's knees, with whetstone in use. It is not Ice or another Valyrian-steel weapon; exact dimensions are not fixed.

Nearby in the command tent: a well-fitted steel field harness with breastplate and backplate, articulated arm and leg defenses, mail protecting gaps, a padded arming garment, practical steel helmet, and gauntlets. All are unworn at the opening. The harness supports ordinary trained movement when donned; coverage, fit, exertion, heat, visibility, and terrain still matter.
Nearby in the command tent: a serviceable dagger and heater shield. Neither is currently carried or readied; shield use does not combine freely with a two-handed sword grip.

Nearby with personal travel gear in the command tent: saddlebag, cloak, blanket, waterskin, mess kit, and flint and steel. Waterskin contents and food or consumable reserves are not quantified. No purse balance is granted.

One campaign riding horse with saddle, bridle, and ordinary tack assigned to Ned at the northern picket line. It is not in immediate reach; reaching it or having it brought takes a plausible action and time. Name, breed, special temperament, armor, and additional mounts are not established.
Ice is inherited House Stark property under Ned's lordship; physical location and availability in the Trident camp are not established.

adjudication.Growth and agency: Starting differences are explicit player-authored premises. Future growth needs causal practice, instruction, or experience and recorded development; plans alone grant no expertise. Personality and decisions remain the player's, with no automatic return to canonical Eddard.
adjudication.Known uncertainty: Exact calendar date within 283 AC.; Exact royal battle plan.; Exact reliable enemy numbers and order of battle unless established through in-world intelligence.; The outcome of the coming battle.; Ned's own survival, wounds, capture status, or future route.; Lyanna's precise whereabouts and condition.; Any later canon event after this starting moment.
adjudication.Major advantages: Legitimate Lord of Winterfell with direct authority over the northern contingent.; Long-term noble martial education.; Player-authored expert longsword and northern field skills, strong battlefield leadership, logistics, geography, and old-gods knowledge. Diplomacy 5, Martial 6, Stewardship 5, and Fieldcraft 7 are supported by the recorded existing skills; narrower abilities retain their limits.; Already tested in a major battle during the rebellion.; Close personal trust with Robert Baratheon and Jon Arryn.; Recent formal alliance with House Tully through marriage.; Northern army is already in camp and preparing for expected battle.
adjudication.Major limitations: Approximately twenty years old and still in his first great war; his strongest command ratings reflect unusual responsibility rather than decades of campaigning.; Newly succeeded to lordship after catastrophic family losses.; Longsword 7 is an explicit player-authored starting divergence, not a claim that book evidence proves elite swordsmanship; it grants no general mastery of all weapons or automatic victories.; Coalition command is shared; he cannot simply command Arryn, Tully, or Baratheon forces as his own.; Exact enemy plan and reliable detailed strength are not granted automatically.; Armor is not worn at the opening instant.; A great lord's status does not make supplies, horses, guards, or information appear without causal availability.
adjudication.Material constraints: Army is in the field on the eve of battle; exact supply state and personal money are unquantified. Listed field equipment is available at its stated location and armor is unworn. Horse is at the northern picket line. Nighttime and nearby enemy forces limit preparation; no automatic protection, supplies, or instant transport.
adjudication.Political vulnerabilities: Open rebel against the reigning king.; Rickard and Brandon are dead, leaving House Stark's adult leadership thinned.; Lyanna remains missing.; The Tully alliance is new and partly secured through marriage politics.; Failure or death at the Trident could place northern command and Stark succession under severe strain.
adjudication.Relevant training: Longsword, two-handed sword, and ordinary noble weapons; Shield and armored fighting; Mounted combat and riding; Frontline and formation leadership; Tactics and campaign logistics; Noble law, heraldry, literacy, and protocol; General fieldcraft and camp life
adjudication.Social leverage: Authority over House Stark's bannermen and northern troops.; Foster-brother bond with Robert.; Foster-son relationship with Jon Arryn.; Marriage tie to Hoster Tully through Catelyn.; Personal credibility from bringing the northern host south and helping at the Battle of the Bells.
adjudication.Starting build support: The user authorized supporting established-skill increases and suitable anchors to realize Diplomacy 5, Martial 6, Stewardship 5, and Fieldcraft 7 while preserving all explicitly named narrower ratings. Thirteen additional existing skills were raised; no new skill, derived anchor, exceptional aptitude, invented biography, or retrospective training award was added.
adjudication.Untrained or weakly trained areas: Sophisticated espionage and manipulation; Professional medicine or surgery; Professional crafts such as armorsmithing or weaponsmithing; Specialized siege engineering; Naval warfare; High-level scholarly fields and foreign languages not otherwise established; Elite archery

background_details.Court experience: Long residence in Jon Arryn's household at the Eyrie; exposure to high nobility; attendance at the tourney at Harrenhal. Limited evidence of prolonged royal-court experience.
background_details.Education: Noble education appropriate to a son of House Stark, including literacy, heraldry, law/custom, riding, arms, command, household obligations, and courtly conduct.
background_details.Important past events: Fosterage at the Eyrie; friendship with Robert; tourney at Harrenhal; disappearance of Lyanna with Rhaegar Targaryen; executions of Rickard and Brandon; Aerys's demand for Ned's and Robert's heads; dangerous return north through the Mountains of the Moon, the Bite, and the Three Sisters; succession as Lord of Winterfell; raising the northern banners; Battle of the Bells; recent marriage to Catelyn Tully at Riverrun.
background_details.Military experience: Formal noble martial training from childhood; active service throughout Robert's Rebellion; called the banners of the North; marched south with the northern host; participated as a commander in the Battle of the Bells, where the rebel relief force helped reverse the battle.
background_details.Religious background: Keeps the old gods of the First Men.
background_details.Trade / occupation: Landed noble and military commander. No skilled trade is established.
background_details.Upbringing: Raised at Winterfell until age eight, then fostered at the Eyrie under Lord Jon Arryn. Robert Baratheon was his fellow ward and became his close friend. From sixteen onward Ned divided time between Winterfell and the Eyrie.
